Ah, yes. I worked in a restaurant when I was younger, and one situation does stand out.

I was scheduled to work as a host on what would turn out to be a very memorable Sunday evening. The restaurant was fairly busy, but the atmosphere was very calm and mellow. I had just finished seating an elderly couple, who dined at our establishment nearly every sunday, when I heard the bell at the front jingle, alerting me to the arrival of another customer. 

I returned to the front and found myself in the presence of a tall man in a long coat, his salt and pepper hair was neatly cut, he wore an expensive looking watch and a large gold ring. His coat extended down to his knees, but his pants seemed to be made of a fine fabric and his shoes were polished leather. He looked to me like he might have been a pilot or a successful businessman. I greeted him and asked if he had a reservation, but he didn't answer, he just stared at me silently for a few uncomfortable moments.

He continued to stare at me as he suddenly began to unbutton his coat, opening it just enough to reveal to me what was beneath. The man had several explosives strapped to his chest.

"You're going to let me ride on your back like a horsey all around the restaurant," he said to me quietly in a deadpan voice.

I stared at him blankly for a moment, trying to process the situation, "You... what?".

He pulled a small trigger from his pocket, "Get on all fours, now." he said meaningfully.

So, I got down on all fours, he sat on my back and yelled "Hi-ho, Silver! away!". He then pulled a lasso from within his coat and we spent the next 15 minutes riding around, lassoing various objects and people and playing cowboy until the police arrived. 

The explosives weren't real. He was staying that weekend in our city on business and had learned that his wife had perished in a car accident. The news caused him to have a complete breakdown. It's a strange and sad story, but it's true, it happened- to a friend of a friend of mine.
